question: Arašidy jeme ako oriešky, no rastlina má zvláštny zvyk. Kvitne nad zemou, ale svoje struky nechá dozrieť niekde inde. Kde?
source_excerpt: This peg grows into the soil, allowing the fruit to develop underground.

extra.why_interesting: Slovaks snack on arašidy all the time and picture them growing on a tree or bush like other 'nuts'. In fact the plant flowers in the air and then buries its own fruit, which is the 'huh, really?' twist.
extra.verification_notes: Peanut flowers above ground, then the peg grows into the soil and pods mature underground (geocarpy), per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut.

explanation: Po odkvitnutí sa stopka kvetu predĺži, ohne sa k zemi a zavŕta sa do pôdy, kde struk dozrie. Preto arašid nie je orech, ale strukovina, rovnako ako hrach či fazuľa.

question: Imelo, ktoré na Vianoce vešiame nad dvere, nerastie v zemi, ale vysoko na konároch stromov. Kto mu tam semienka vynesie?
source_excerpt: spread depends mainly on thrush-family birds; seeds that pass through a bird's digestive tract germinate sooner

extra.why_interesting: Everyone in Slovakia hangs imelo over the door at Christmas, but few wonder how a plant ends up high in a treetop without ever touching the ground. The player can reason it out ('what visits branches and eats berries?'), which makes it a satisfying 'I worked it out!' moment.
extra.verification_notes: Mistletoe seeds are dispersed by birds, chiefly thrushes, per Czech botanical flora (https://files.ibot.cas.cz/cevs/images/taxa/kvetena_cr/Viscum.pdf).

explanation: Vtáky, napríklad drozdy, zjedia lepkavé biele bobule a semienko potom vylúčia alebo si ho otrú z zobáka o konár, kde sa prilepí. Imelo potom zapustí korene priamo do dreva a ťahá zo stromu vodu.
